extracted.intended_audience: researchers (authors of preprints), potential recommenders/editors, and journals interested in PCI recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and standards for evaluating and recommending preprints within the Peer Community In (PCI) network and for publishing PCI-recommended articles in the Peer Community Journal (PCJ). Covers review process, transparency, reproducibility, conflict-of-interest rules, and open-access publication options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous evaluations by at least two reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions made by editors (called recommenders at PCI) are based on rigorous evaluations by at least two reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes that editorial decisions rely on multiple rigorous evaluations; this is a minimum-reviewer standard for the PCI process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing Board quality check and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Managing Board of each PCI, composed of established researchers who volunteer their time, checks the quality of reviews and validates all editorial decisions and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All editorial decisions and recommendations are subject to an additional layer of oversight by a managing board to ensure review quality and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on soundness, quality and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI and Peer Community Journal focus their policies on the soundness of scientific questions and the quality and reproducibility of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations prioritize methodological soundness and reproducibility rather than journal-based prestige metrics; this guides reviewers' assessment criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require deposition of articles' data, code, and scripts in open repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles evaluated by PCI (preprints), as well as the associated data, code, and scripts, must be deposited in open access repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-data/code requirement is enforced to support reproducibility; reviewers and recommendations assume access to underlying materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of PCI evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: For accepted preprints, PCI evaluations are also publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review reports/evaluations are published alongside the preprint to increase transparency and allow readers to inspect the review rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of financial conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI prohibits financial conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial conflicts are not allowed in the PCI process; this is a strict policy intended to preserve impartiality of reviewers and recommenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require justification of sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI requires justification of the sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must justify their sample size decisions (power, design) as part of the evaluation criteria; this supports rigorous statistical and experimental assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage preregistrations, Registered Reports, replication and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI encourages the use of preregistrations and Registered Reports, the replication of studies and the publication of negative results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These practices are actively promoted as desirable for improving research reliability and reducing publication bias; reviewers are expected to value these practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a detailed auto-questionnaire of evaluation to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI provides to authors a detailed auto-questionnaire of evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The auto-questionnaire guides authors on what reviewers will examine and helps structure submissions to meet PCI evaluation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer pilot data and script editing in some PCIs
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI offers pilot data and script editing in two PCIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted support (editing of pilot data and scripts) is available in some thematic PCIs to help authors meet reproducibility and code-quality expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence, non-profit and free process
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI and Peer Community Journal are non-profit, non-commercial, independent, managed by scientists for scientists, and the entire process is free for any user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These organizational values shape policies: accessibility, low cost to authors/readers, and governance by scientist volunteers rather than commercial publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open infrastructure and open-source software
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI infrastructure is open source and the initiative is embedded in Open-Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-source infrastructure and open-science alignment are part of the platform's standards to promote transparency and reusability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoupling evaluation from publication; transferability of recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI decouples evaluation and publication: an article recommended by a PCI may subsequently be published in Peer Community Journal or in any other journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PCI recommendation is a public validation; authors can leave the preprint on servers, publish in PCJ (diamond OA) free of charge, or submit to PCI-friendly or other journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended preprints become citable validated outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon positive evaluation, the PCIs validate and publicly recommend preprints, making them complete, reliable, and citable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation is intended to signal that the work has passed PCI's quality checks and is suitable for citation and further dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommenders are established researcher volunteers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommenders (editors) are established researchers who volunteer their time to manage reviews and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial roles are filled by active researchers; this shapes expectations for expertise and community-driven standards in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational scaling by focusing on essential workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Scalability is achieved by focusing on the essential workload required for the production and distribution of knowledge and by distributing it across a broad network of researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI emphasizes minimizing unnecessary administrative burden while maintaining rigorous review standards to allow growth without compromising quality.
